questions.question: Explain how advertising warns against imitation.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how advertising warns against imitation. / [CO1]
  • Advertising uses "Brand Protection" strategies. By highlighting distinct brand assets (logos,
  • unique packaging) and emphasizing "The Original," ads train consumers to use visual
  • heuristics to avoid cheaper, low-quality substitutes.Advertising emphasizes unique brand
  • markers, trademarks, and "genuine" labels to differentiate from counterfeits. Advertisements
  • include disclaimers (e.g., “Do not try this at home”) to prevent unsafe imitation, especially in
  • risky scenes (stunts, driving, etc.).Also by protecting brand identity
  • (counterfeiting) and preventing behavioral mimicry (safety).

questions.question: Describe how self-esteem affects consumer decisions.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how self-esteem affects consumer decisions.
  • Ans- Self-esteem significantly influences consumer decisions by shaping how individuals
  • perceive themselves and what they believe will enhance their self-image. People with high self-
  • esteem tend to make confident, autonomous choices and often seek products that reflect their
  • identity or personal values. In contrast, those with low self-esteem may be more influenced by
  • external opinions, advertising, or trends, choosing products that they believe will boost their self-
  • worth or gain social approval. Thus, self-esteem impacts not only what consumers buy, but also
  • why they buy it.

  • language makes a slogan easier to process and remember, increasing its mental availability.
